abstract: Nippon Hoso Kyokai (NHK, Japan Broadcasting Corporation), has developed a new artificial intelligence (AI)-driven broadcasting technology called “Smart Production” designed to quickly and accurately gather and analyze diverse types of social information and deliver information to a wide range of viewers. Smart Production uses AI to analyze information obtained from social media and open data as well as the know-how related to program production possessed by broadcast stations. This approach makes it possible to extract events and incidents in society and present the results of the analysis to producers. In particular, image analysis technology for recognizing objects in video and speech recognition technology for generating transcripts of interviews enable metadata to be automatically generated for video footage. Additionally, research and development are progressing on technology for automatically converting broadcast data into content that can be easily understood by viewers with special needs.

authors.bio: Hiroyuki Kaneko received BE and ME degrees in electric and electronics engineering from Sophia University, Tokyo, Japan, in 2000 and 2002, respectively. He joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) in 2002. He has been engaged in research of computer graphics-based content production technology, especially on sign language animation in NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories (STRL), Tokyo, since 2006.
authors.name: Hiroyuki Kaneko

authors.bio: Jun Goto received BE and ME degrees in electrical engineering from Tokushima University, Tokushima, Japan, in 1991 and 1993, respectively. He joined NHK in 1993 and has been with NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Tokyo, Japan since 1998. He received a PhD in informatics from the Graduate University for Advanced Study, Hayama, Japan, in 2014. He is currently a senior research engineer at NHK-STRL. His research interests include big data analysis and information extraction based on natural language processing.
authors.name: Jun Goto

authors.bio: Yoshihiko Kawai is a senior manager with NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Tokyo, Japan. He received a PhD degree in engineering from Osaka University, Suita, Japan. His research interests include multimedia processing and video indexing. He is a member of the Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers (IEICE) and the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers (ITE), Japan.
authors.name: Yoshihiko Kawai

authors.bio: Takahiro Mochizuki received BE and ME degrees from the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, Japan, in 1994 and 1996, and the PhD degree in engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology in 2010. He was with the Outside Broadcasting Technical Division of NHK from 1996 to 1998. Since 1998, he has been working on image processing and recognition with NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Tokyo. His current research focuses on development of video summarization technologies.
authors.name: Takahiro Mochizuki

authors.bio: Shoei Sato received BE and ME degrees from Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan, in 1993. He also received a DrEng degree from Waseda University, Tokyo, Japan, in 2008. From 1995, he was with NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Tokyo. He is currently a senior research engineer with NHK Engineering Systems Inc., Tokyo, and is engaged in speech recognition research for broadcasting. He contributed to the development of live closed-captioning system using speech recognition.
authors.name: Shoei Sato

authors.bio: Atsushi Imai received BE degree in electrical engineering from Saitama University, Saitama, Japan, in 1989, and the PhD degree from the University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan, in 2014. He joined NHK in 1989. Since 1992, he has been with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories. He is currently a senior research engineer with NHK Engineering Systems Inc., Tokyo. His research interests include the analysis of the hearing and speaking, and the design of aid devices for the disabled
authors.name: Atsushi Imai

authors.bio: Yuko Yamanouchi received a BE degree in electronic engineering from Sophia University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1986, and ME and PhD degrees in electronic engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, in 1988 and 2005, respectively. She joined NHK in 1988. Since 1990, she has been with NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Tokyo, and she is currently the head of the Smart Production Research Division. She has been engaged in research on image processing and computer graphics technique for TV program production.
authors.name: Yuko Yamanouchi
